sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A QUASI ZONAL UPPER PATTERN WILL PERSIST OVER THE U.S. SATURDAY WITH PRIMARY BELT OF WLYS OVER NRN THIRD OF THE COUNTRY. UPPER LOW NOW CENTERED OVER SRN BRITISH COLUMBIA WILL SHIFT VERY SLOWLY EWD...WHILE DOWNSTREAM UPPER LOW CONTINUES THROUGH SRN QUEBEC. A CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED VORT MAX OVER THE CNTRL/NRN PLAINS WILL ADVANCE THROUGH THE UPPER/MID MS VALLEY REGION. AT THE SURFACE A QUASISTATIONARY FRONT WILL PERSIST FROM A SURFACE LOW IN SWRN KS EWD INTO THE MID MS VALLEY. COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE THROUGH ND IN ASSOCIATION WITH IMPULSES ROTATING THROUGH SWRN CANADA UPPER LOW. FARTHER EAST...A COLD FRONT SHOULD MOVE OFF THE MID ATLANTIC SEABOARD WITH TRAILING PORTIONS ADVANCING SWD INTO SRN PORTIONS OF THE SERN STATES.

sections.title: MID MS VALLEY AREA
sections.text: WEAKENING MCS AND ATTENDANT VORT MAX CURRENTLY OVER NEB AND SD WILL ADVANCE INTO IA AND SRN MN BY 12Z SATURDAY. OTHER MORE ELEVATED STORMS MAY ALSO DEVELOP AND BE IN PROGRESS WITHIN WARM ADVECTION ZONE FROM ERN MO INTO IL. SLY BOUNDARY LAYER FLOW EAST OF KS LEE LOW WILL MAINTAIN INFLUX OF RICHER MOISTURE BENEATH STEEPER LAPSE RATE PLUME. ATMOSPHERE WILL LIKELY BECOME MODERATELY TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE OVER THE MID MS VALLEY SOUTH OF CONVECTIVE DEBRIS. THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR ADDITIONAL STORMS TO DEVELOP ALONG THE PERIPHERY OF MORNING CONVECTION OR RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES AND ON ERN EDGE OF EML ACROSS SRN IA INTO NRN MO AS THE ATMOSPHERE DESTABILIZES. ACTIVITY WILL SUBSEQUENTLY DEVELOP SEWD THROUGH THE MIDDLE MS VALLEY AND EVENTUALLY WRN PORTIONS OF TN VALLEY. SELY LOW LEVEL FLOW VEERING TO WNWLY WITH HEIGHT WILL RESULT IN 40-50 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR WITH POTENTIAL FOR A FEW SUPERCELLS BEFORE STORMS EVOLVE INTO AN MCS. PRIMARY THREATS WILL BE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND...BUT ISOLATED TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT BEFORE STORMS GROW UPSCALE. THREAT SHOULD DECREASE TOWARD MID EVENING AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES.

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS AREA
sections.text: IN WAKE OF FRIDAYS MCS...THE ATMOSPHERE SHOULD ONCE AGAIN BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE IN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR AND OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS WHERE SELY LOW LEVEL FLOW WILL MAINTAIN UPPER 50S DEWPOINTS BENEATH STEEP LAPSE RATES. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WY AND INTENSIFY AS THEY SPREAD EWD THROUGH THE HIGH PLAINS WHERE RICHER MOISTURE WILL RESIDE AND WHERE 40-45 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR WILL PROMOTE A FEW SUPERCELLS. ACTIVITY MAY EVENTUALLY EVOLVE INTO AN MCS AS IT CONTINUES EWD. OTHER STORMS MAY ALSO DEVELOP FARTHER NEWD INTO ND ALONG COLD FRONT. PRIMARY THREATS WILL BE ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND BEFORE ACTIVITY WEAKENS TOWARD MID-LATE EVENING.

sections.title: SERN STATES
sections.text: SCATTERED MULTICELL AND PULSE STORMS WILL LIKELY REDEVELOP OVER THE SERN STATES ALONG AND SOUTH OF FRONT FROM CNTRL/SRN AL EWD THROUGH SRN GA AND THE COASTAL CAROLINAS. THE FRONT WILL HAVE SHIFTED SOUTH OF THE STRONGER FLOW ALOFT AND FRIDAYS WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING SUGGEST THE ATMOSPHERE MAY NOT BECOME QUITE AS UNSTABLE. WHILE ISOLATED DOWNBURSTS WINDS MAY OCCUR WITH THE STRONGER STORMS...OVERALL COVERAGE OF SEVERE EVENTS IS NOT EXPECTED TO BECOME SUFFICIENT FOR MORE THAN 5% PROBABILITIES. ..DIAL/LEITMAN.. 06/25/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER PARTS OF THE NRN PLNS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... MODERATE WSW TO WNW FLOW WILL PREVAIL OVER THE CNTRL/NRN RCKYS...THE NRN HALF OF THE PLNS...AND THE MID/UPR MS VLY REGION THIS PERIOD AS RIDGE SLOWLY AMPLIFIES OVER THE SRN PLNS. UPR LOW NOW ENTERING SRN AB SHOULD CONTINUE ENE INTO SK...WHILE DOWNSTREAM LOW WEAKENS IN QUEBEC. A CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED VORT NOW OVER IA SHOULD TURN ESE ACROSS THE MID MS VLY. AT LWR LVLS...A QSTNRY FRONT LIKELY WILL PERSIST FROM STNRY LEE LOW IN WRN KS E AND SE INTO THE LWR MS/TN VLYS. AND...A WEAK COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE SLOWLY SE ACROSS ND IN ASSOCIATION WITH PASSING DISTURBANCES IN WSWLY UPR FLOW. FARTHER EAST...A WEAK COLD FRONT/LEE TROUGH SHOULD MOVE OFF THE MID ATLANTIC CST...WITH TRAILING PORTION ADVANCING S ACROSS PARTS OF THE CAROLINAS/GA/AL.

sections.title: LWR MO/MID MS/LWR TN VLYS TODAY/TNGT
sections.text: LWR MO VLY MCS AND ATTENDANT CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED VORT MAX SHOULD TURN MORE S OF E ACROSS MO LATER THIS MORNING. ADDITIONAL STORMS SHOULD FORM AHEAD OF THE MCS OVER MO AND PERHAPS FAR ERN KS TODAY AS MOIST/SLY LOW LVL FLOW PERSISTS BENEATH EML. OTHER STORMS MAY CONTINUE TO FORM ON ERN EDGE OF EML FROM ERN MO AND SRN IL SSE INTO WRN KY/WRN TN. STRONG SFC HEATING SHOULD BOOST SBCAPE TO AOA 3000 J/KG...AND S TO SELY LOW LVL FLOW BENEATH 40 KT WNW TO NWLY MID LVL JET WILL YIELD 40-50 KT DEEP NWLY SHEAR. THUS...SETUP SHOULD BECOME FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL AND DMGG WIND. SOME OF THE STORMS ALMOST CERTAINLY WILL EVOLVE INTO FORWARD-PROPAGATING SEGMENTS AND BOWS...WITH AN INCREASING THREAT FOR DMGG WIND BY LATER IN THE DAY INTO EARLY TNGT. GIVEN LOW LVL VEERING PROFILES AND FAIRLY RICH MOISTURE...SOME THREAT ALSO WILL EXIST FOR TORNADOES...MAINLY BEFORE UPSCALE DEVELOPMENT OCCURS. THE SVR THREAT SHOULD DECREASE TOWARD MID EVE AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES/CINH INCREASES.

sections.title: NRN PLNS THIS AFTN INTO TNGT
sections.text: IN WAKE OF OVERNIGHT MCS...CONSIDERABLE DESTABILIZATION SHOULD OCCUR TODAY FROM THE WRN DAKOTAS SW INTO SE MT/ERN WY...ALONG AND AHEAD OF AFOREMENTIONED COLD FRONT. WEAK LOW LVL SE FLOW WILL MAINTAIN UPR 50S F SFC DEWPOINTS BENEATH NRN FRINGE OF EML ASSOCIATED WITH SRN PLNS RIDGE. SCTD STORMS SHOULD ONCE AGAIN FORM MAINLY OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WY...SRN MT...AND THE BLACK HILLS...AND ALONG THE FRONT. THE STORMS SHOULD STRENGTHEN AS THEY MOVE E INTO RICHER MOISTURE...WHERE 40-45 KT WLY DEEP SHEAR WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS WITH HAIL AND DMGG WIND. THE ACTIVITY MAY EVOLVE INTO ONE OR TWO SMALL CLUSTERS THIS EVE. THESE SHOULD MOVE GENERALLY E OR ESE TOWARD THE LWR PLNS LATER TNGT...WITH A DIMINISHING THREAT FOR SVR.

sections.title: SE U.S. THIS AFTN
sections.text: SCTD MULTICELL AND PULSE STORMS LIKELY WILL FORM ALONG WEAK FRONT/TROUGH OVER THE CAROLINA CSTL PLN AND SRN PARTS OF GA/AL TODAY...MAINLY S OF WHERE SIGNIFICANT CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING OCCURRED ON FRIDAY. UPR FLOW ACROSS REGION WILL BE RATHER WEAK...BUT SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW SUSTAINED STORMS/STORM CLUSTERS THAT COULD YIELD LOCALLY DMGG WIND.

sections.title: SERN NY/SW NE ENGLAND THIS AFTN
sections.text: A FEW SMALL CLUSTERS OF STORMS MAY FORM THIS AFTN OVER CNTRL/SRN PARTS OF THE HUDSON VLY AS MODEST SFC HEATING OCCURS AHEAD OF UPR VORT APPROACHING FROM SRN ONT/WRN NY. WEAK LOW TO MID LVL LAPSE RATES SHOULD LIMIT STORM STRENGTH. BUT A FEW STORMS COULD YIELD MARGINALLY SVR HAIL EWD INTO WRN MA/CT GIVEN COOL THERMAL PROFILES AND CO-LOCATION OF FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH AXIS OF GREATEST DESTABILIZATION. ..CORFIDI/GRAMS.. 06/25/2011

sections.title: LOWER MO VALLEY INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY AND CNTRL GULF STATES
sections.text: RADAR DATA SUGGEST THAT NOCTURNAL MCS ONGOING OVER MO HAS GENERATED A CONVECTIVELY INDUCED MCV WHICH SHOULD CONTINUE TO TRANSLATE EWD INTO IL TODAY. FORCING ALONG THE SRN PERIPHERY OF THIS FEATURE COMBINED WITH CONVERGENCE ALONG AGGREGATE CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW-SYNOPTIC FRONTAL BOUNDARY...EXTENDING FROM E-CNTRL KS THROUGH CNTRL MO AND FAR WRN KY INTO MIDDLE TN...WILL FOCUS THE MOST INTENSE TSTM ACTIVITY THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. AIR MASS ALONG AND S OF THIS BOUNDARY IS QUITE MOIST WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S AND LOWER 70S. WHEN COUPLED WITH DAYTIME HEATING AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...ENVIRONMENT IS EXPECTED TO BECOME MODERATELY TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE BY AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE INCREASING TO 2000-3500 J/KG. CURRENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT ONGOING STORMS OVER CNTRL MO SHOULD CONTINUE TO INTENSIFY THIS AFTERNOON WITH ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT LIKELY ALONG ABOVE-MENTIONED BAROCLINIC ZONE. KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS AND BOW ECHO-TYPE STORM STRUCTURES WITH ATTENDANT RISKS OF A TORNADO OR TWO...LARGE HAIL AND CORRIDORS OF WIND DAMAGE FROM THE OZARKS INTO LOWER OH VALLEY. FOR ADDITIONAL NEAR-TERM GUIDANCE ON THIS AREA...SEE MCD 1382. MEANWHILE...DOWNSTREAM TSTM CLUST

sections.title: DAKOTAS/NEB/WY
sections.text: SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED 50-60 KT MIDLEVEL JET STREAK OVER THE NRN ROCKIES WILL TRANSLATE NEWD INTO SRN SASKATCHEWAN BY THIS EVENING WITH SRN FRINGE OF STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT GLANCING REGION NEAR THE PEAK OF THE DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE. THIS COUPLED WITH CONVERGENCE ALONG COLD FRONT SETTLING SEWD THROUGH THE WRN DAKOTAS AND ASCENT ALONG FAVORED TERRAIN WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED TSTMS LATER THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. ELY LOW-LEVEL WIND COMPONENT OWING TO WEAK LOW PRESSURE OVER ERN WY WILL MAINTAIN 50S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS BENEATH NRN EXTENSION OF EML...RESULTING IN MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-2500 J/KG. THIS INSTABILITY WILL COINCIDE WITHIN A KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT FEATURING VERTICALLY VEERING WIND PROFILES WITH 35-45 KT OF DEEP WLY SHEAR. AS SUCH THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR SUPERCELLS WITH THE PRIMARY HAZARDS BEING LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. ..MEAD/COHEN.. 06/25/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS AREA
sections.text: ...OZARKS/MID MS/LOWER OH/TN VALLEY REGIONS... SEWD/SWD STORM PROPAGATION WITH MID MS VALLEY CONVECTION APPEARS LESS LIKELY ATTM...AND THUS HAVE TRIMMED SLIGHT RISK NWWD IN THE MS/AL REGION. ELSEWHERE...EXPECT AN INCREASE IN CONVECTION TO OCCUR FROM SERN KS ACROSS MO LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING IN THE WAKE OF ONGOING STORMS. AS POST-CONVECTIVE AIRMASS RECOVERS...INSTABILITY -- IN CONJUNCTION WITH AMPLE EXISTING SHEAR -- SUPPORTS CONTINUATION OF THE SLIGHT RISK FORECAST. SEVERAL MODELS SUGGEST DEVELOPMENT OF AN MCS LATER THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT...WITH SEWD/SWD MOVEMENT ACROSS MO -- AND POSSIBLY INTO NRN AR -- EXPECTED.

sections.title: NRN PLAINS AREA
sections.text: INCREASING CU EVIDENT FROM WRN ND SWD INTO SRN/ERN WY ATTM REVEALS CORRESPONDING INCREASE IN LARGE-SCALE UVV...WITH FORECAST FOR SCATTERED STORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THIS REGION STILL ON TRACK. DESTABILIZATION ONGOING COMBINED WITH SUFFICIENT SHEAR INDICATED ACROSS THIS REGION SUPPORTS CONTINUATION OF SLIGHT RISK FORECAST IN THIS AREA. ..GOSS.. 06/25/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1129 AM CDT SAT JUN 25 2011/

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: ...LOWER MO VALLEY/OZARKS/MIDDLE MS VALLEY... GIVEN A NOCTURNALLY COOLING BOUNDARY LAYER AND WEAK FORCING/RISING HEIGHTS IN THE WAKE OF A SHORTWAVE TROUGH/MCV NEAR THE MS RIVER EARLY THIS EVENING...WARM SECTOR/SURFACE BASED DEVELOPMENT SEEMS UNLIKELY ESPECIALLY WITH WESTWARD EXTENT ACROSS THE LOWER MO VALLEY/OZARKS. THAT SAID...SOME WINDOW WILL EXIST THIS EVENING FOR A SURFACE BASED SUPERCELL CAPABLE OF A TORNADO FROM CENTRAL/SOUTHEAST MO INTO FAR SOUTHERN IL. OTHERWISE...AIDED BY THE AFOREMENTIONED MID LEVEL IMPULSE AND A NOCTURNALLY INCREASING LOW LEVEL JET...THE MOST LIKELY SCENARIO IS FOR STRONG/SEVERE STORMS TO CONTINUE TO INCREASE THIS EVENING ALONG AND N/NE OF AN OUTFLOW REINFORCED WARM FRONT. IN ADDITION TO BOUTS OF SEVERE HAIL...STORMS MAY ULTIMATELY GROW UPSCALE INTO AN MCS WITH DAMAGING WINDS A CONCERN AS WELL LATER THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS WILL CONTINUE TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE THROUGH EARLY/MID EVENING IN VICINITY OF AN E/SE ADVANCING COLD FRONT...FROM WESTERN/NORTHERN NEB INTO THE DAKOTAS. THE 00Z OBSERVED SOUNDING FROM RAPID CITY REFLECTED A VERY FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC/KINEMATIC PROFILE FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL/PERHAPS A TORNADO EARLY THIS EVENING...WITH MLCAPE UPWARDS OF 3000 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AROUND 55 KT. ONE OR MORE CLUSTERS MAY ULTIMATELY EVOLVE THIS EVENING ACROSS NORTHERN NEB AND/OR SD WITH DAMAGING WINDS POSSIBLE. ..GUYER.. 06/26/2011
